title: Create Table [NOT NULL]
description:
Have you noticed that you can insert _**empty**_ values into tables? Sometimes, this is a problem, as you may have required fields, and you would just need the backend to verify, adding complexity. This is what `NOT NULL` is for. It makes sure a field _cannot be null_. You put it _after the datatype_.
## Assignment:
BWS needs the customers table's name and plan fields to be non-null! Fix it.
runHarness:
INSERT INTO customers (name, plan) VALUES ('Tim', 'cheapest');
SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='customers';
